slots.practicalActivity: In the Oracle Fusion practice environment, navigate from the Navigator into the General Accounting work area and open the Reports and Analytics pane, noting which of the four reporting jobs (formatted statements, ad hoc exploration, pixel-perfect scheduled output, Excel-native analysis) each visible tile or folder seems to serve. Then write a one-line mapping of Financial Reporting Studio, OTBI, BI Publisher and Smart View to the specific reader -- board member, collections analyst, compliance team, controller -- each one is built for.
slots.deliverable: A written mapping of the four Oracle Fusion reporting tools to the four reader types they serve, based on exploring the live Reports and Analytics pane.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the reporting-tool decision chart, write out which tool you'd pick for three new reporting requests of your own (a statutory balance sheet, an ad hoc aging check, a scheduled 1099 form) and justify each choice in one sentence. Then, in the practice environment, review your own user's duty roles and record which subject areas or reporting folders you can currently see, connecting the security model to what you can actually access.
slots.deliverable: A written tool-choice justification for three reporting requests, plus a recorded list of the subject areas or folders visible under your own security access.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Reporting Overview: write a one-paragraph recommendation memo for a hypothetical client who says "I just need my monthly financials" -- naming which of the four tools you'd start them with and why, referencing the four reporting jobs and reader types from Lesson 1. Then locate, in the practice environment, where each of the four tools is actually launched from (General Accounting work area, Reports and Analytics catalog, Scheduled Processes, Excel ribbon) and confirm you can navigate to each starting point.
slots.deliverable: A client-facing recommendation memo for first-time reporting, plus a confirmed navigation path to each of the four tools' starting points.

slots.practicalActivity: In your Oracle Fusion practice environment, open the Financial Reporting Center from the General Accounting work area and identify each content type on the page -- Financial Reporting Web Studio reports, Account Groups, Smart View reports, OTBI content, BI Publisher reports. Run one seeded financial report (such as a standard Trial Balance) by selecting a real point of view (ledger and period), then open an Account Group and view its Sunburst visualization, recording what account set it's monitoring.
slots.deliverable: A documented tour of the Financial Reporting Center's content types, one seeded report run against a real point of view, and notes on one Account Group's Sunburst view.

slots.practicalActivity: In Financial Reporting Web Studio, build the course's three-line summary report from scratch: a Total Revenue row referencing the revenue hierarchy's parent node, a Total Expenses row referencing the expense hierarchy's parent node, and a Net Result formula row (Row 1 minus Row 2), with a single Actual column. Set the point of view to a real ledger and period, preview it, confirm the title updates automatically when you change periods, then save and publish it to the Financial Reporting Center.
slots.deliverable: A saved and published three-row Financial Reporting Studio report (Revenue, Expenses, Net Result) visible in the Financial Reporting Center.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for the Financial Reporting Center: take the report you published in the previous slot, change its point of view to a different period, rerun it, and confirm the header text updates to the new period automatically rather than showing a stale hard-coded label. Then write a short note on the difference between saving a report and publishing it, using your own report as the example.
slots.deliverable: A re-run version of your published report under a different point of view with a verified auto-updating header, plus a written save-versus-publish explanation.

slots.practicalActivity: In OTBI, open the Payables subject area and identify its facts (invoice amount, days overdue) and dimensions (supplier, invoice status, due date) by browsing the folder structure. Then build a new analysis listing unpaid invoices over $10,000 -- the course's running example -- choosing the right facts and dimensions, and add a results-table view plus a prompt that lets a viewer change the dollar threshold at run time.
slots.deliverable: A saved OTBI analysis of unpaid invoices over $10,000 with a user-adjustable dollar-threshold prompt.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a second small OTBI analysis showing total payables by supplier, then create a dashboard with two pages, placing both analyses side by side in a column on one page. Add a dashboard-level Business Unit prompt that filters both analyses at once, and record whether changing it updates both. Finally, schedule the unpaid-invoices analysis to run on a recurring basis.
slots.deliverable: A two-page OTBI dashboard combining the unpaid-invoices and total-payables-by-supplier analyses under one shared Business Unit prompt, with the underlying analysis scheduled to run recurringly.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for OTBI Analyses and Dashboards: document the exact scheduling screen and delivery options available for your unpaid-invoices analysis, and separately write a plan for embedding that same analysis directly inside the Payables work area landing page rather than only living in the standalone catalog, naming which specific dashboard or analysis would need to move and why.
slots.deliverable: A documented OTBI scheduling/delivery configuration for the unpaid-invoices analysis, plus a written plan for embedding it inside the Payables work area.

slots.practicalActivity: Compare a BI Publisher candidate report (a 1099-style form) against an OTBI candidate (a quick ad hoc list) and write one sentence justifying why each belongs to its own tool, grounded in the "pixel-perfect" distinction. Then build a simple BI Publisher data model with one query against Payables data, confirm it produces sample XML, and build an RTF template in the Template Builder add-in with a header area and one looping detail table mapped to that XML.
slots.deliverable: A written pixel-perfect-vs-ad-hoc justification, a working BI Publisher data model producing sample XML, and an RTF template rendering that data correctly in preview.

lessons.title: Running and Scheduling BI Publisher Reports

slots.practicalActivity: Schedule the finished report from the previous slot to run once, and download its output in two different formats (PDF and Excel) to confirm the same data model and template support multiple output formats. Then pick one common financial report type from the lesson -- a 1099 form, a check-stub layout, or an aging report -- and identify, in the Reports and Analytics catalog, the seeded BI Publisher report closest to it.
slots.deliverable: One scheduled BI Publisher report producing output in both PDF and Excel, plus an identified seeded report matching a common financial report type.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for BI Publisher: build one complete financial report end to end in the practice environment -- a fresh data model and a fresh RTF template, not reusing the one from earlier in this chapter -- covering a different common report type (for example an AR aging form instead of the AP form you already built), and run it to confirm both the data and the layout are correct.
slots.deliverable: One complete, independently built BI Publisher report (new data model plus new template) covering a second common financial report type, run successfully.

lessons.title: Ad Hoc Analysis with Smart View

slots.practicalActivity: Install and configure the Smart View add-in in Excel, set up a shared connection to your Fusion practice environment, sign in with your Oracle Fusion credentials, and confirm the setup by connecting to the GL balances cube and pulling back one familiar balance. Then do ad hoc analysis: pivot that balance by period and by cost center directly inside the Excel grid.
slots.deliverable: A working Smart View connection in Excel pulling a real GL balance, pivoted ad hoc by period and cost center.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a small Report Package in Narrative Reporting with two sections (for example an executive summary and a financial statement section), assign yourself as both author and reviewer, draft content in one section, and leave a review comment on the other using Smart View's Word-based review interface. Then refresh one of your Smart View worksheets from the previous slot and note what changed versus the cached version.
slots.deliverable: A two-section Report Package with one authored section and one reviewed Smart View comment, plus one refreshed Smart View worksheet.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Smart View and Excel Reporting: build one Smart View worksheet that pivots ledger balances by ledger, period and account across at least two dimensions, refresh it to confirm it pulls live data rather than a static snapshot, then export or distribute it as you would to a client, and write a short note on which parts of the chapter (setup, ad hoc analysis, Report Packages, or refresh/distribute) a real consultant uses most often week to week.
slots.deliverable: A multi-dimensional Smart View worksheet refreshed against live data and distributed as a deliverable, with a written note on real-world usage frequency.

lessons.title: Financial Statements: Income Statement and Balance Sheet
Trial Balance and Account Analysis Reports

slots.practicalActivity: Run a real Income Statement and Balance Sheet from Financial Reporting Studio for your practice ledger and period, and confirm the Balance Sheet actually balances (Assets = Liabilities + Equity, to the cent) and that retained earnings ties to the prior period's ending balance plus this period's net income. Then run the Trial Balance and an Account Analysis drill-down on any account that looks unusual, and run the Payables Invoice Aging Report, noting which aging bucket holds the largest dollar total.
slots.deliverable: A verified, balancing Income Statement and Balance Sheet pair, a Trial Balance with one Account Analysis drill-down, and a Payables aging report with its largest bucket identified.

lessons.title: Fixed Assets and Cash Management Reports

slots.practicalActivity: Run the Receivables Aging Report and compare its bucket structure to the Payables aging report from the previous slot, then run a Fixed Assets register extract and a Cash Management bank reconciliation report for the same period. Read through the month-end sequence (subledgers closed, then Trial Balance, then reconciliations, then aging, then statements last) and check off, for your own practice ledger, whether each subledger is actually closed before you'd call the close "ready."
slots.deliverable: A Receivables aging report, a Fixed Assets register extract, a Cash Management bank reconciliation, and a completed subledger-closed checklist for your practice ledger.

slots.practicalActivity: Course-closing capstone: run your own full month-end reporting package end to end in the correct sequence -- confirm subledgers closed, run the Trial Balance first and stop to investigate if it doesn't balance, run the Payables-to-Ledger and bank reconciliations, run AP and AR aging, and only then run the Income Statement and Balance Sheet -- documenting each step's result in order. Write a two-paragraph reflection on why running the statements last, after every supporting check is clean, is the actual skill this course was teaching.
slots.deliverable: A fully sequenced, documented month-end reporting package (Trial Balance through final statements) plus a written reflection on close sequencing as the core skill.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can choose and use the right Oracle Fusion reporting tool for the job at hand -- building and publishing Financial Reporting Studio financial statements, creating OTBI ad hoc analyses and dashboards, building BI Publisher pixel-perfect scheduled reports, and producing Smart View ad hoc analysis and Report Packages -- and can assemble a complete, correctly sequenced month-end reporting package.
